title: Aurigence - proxy/sdk compatibility workshop
summary: Customer is evaluating Redwood for low-latency recommendations pipeline. Key concerns: VPC network egress, per-tenant quotas, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter compatibility, and end-to-end observability. Favorable to start with Hosted pilot, but dedicated capacity and private deployment options explored for compliance and predictable throughput.
next_steps: Redwood: Send Dedicated pilot pricing + committed burst add-on
Customer: Share VPC topology and expected QPS by tenant (Mohammed)
Redwood SE: Prepare LangChain adapter proof-of-concept repo with sample prompts (Rina)
Set follow-up technical deep-dive next week to run a mini-benchmark
action_items: Mohammed Khan: Share VPC network diagram and firewall rules by 2027-01-04
Rina Patel: Create LangChain + LlamaIndex starter repo and email link by 2026-12-23
Jamie Park: Send pricing sheet for Hosted/Dedicated/Private with pilot options by 2026-12-22
Diego Alvarez: Draft observability integration notes (tracing headers, token-level cost tags) by 2026-12-28
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Rina Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Aurigence), Mohammed Khan (Platform Eng), Ava Brooks (ML Eng), Samir Desai (Security)

[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick icebreaker — we'll go through where you are today and then drill into the integration points around SDKs, proxies, and observability.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Cool. High level — Aurigence runs a recommendations microservice that talks to multiple models. We're trying to standardize on a provider that can scale per-tenant and give us good visibility into token cost.
[00:27] Mohammed Khan: Yeah, our main constraints: VPC egress limits, per-tenant quotas for fair usage, and we need predictable p95 latency under 300ms for short prompt paths.
[00:41] Rina Patel: Thanks — that's helpful. Two quick clarifications: when you say per-tenant quotas, are those enforced in your proxy or would you want Redwood to keep per-API-key rate limits?
[00:52] Mohammed Khan: Ideally both. We'd like the gateway to do first-line throttling so we avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbor effects, but Redwood's quotas should exist as a second guardrail and for billing.
[01:05] Diego Alvarez: Makes sense. We support token and request-based quotas at the API key level, and you can combine that with your edge gateway rules. On Dedicated and Private we can also surface per-tenant metrics to your SIEM via our observability hooks.
[01:19] Ava Brooks: How intrusive is the SDK? We use LangChain and LlamaIndex heavy in our pipeline — we don't want a big rewrite.
[01:28] Rina Patel: We have lightweight Python and JS SDKs; for LangChain/LlamaIndex we provide adapter examples. Usually it's a thin transport layer: most of your prompt engineering stays the same, you just swap the client and configure streaming/callbacks.
[01:44] Lena Ortiz: Do you have a concrete example?
[01:47] Rina Patel: Yes, I can show the sample. (screen share noise) Here's a simple LangChain LLM wrapper that calls Redwood's /v1/generate endpoint — you pass the request_options, include stop tokens and streaming callbacks. For LlamaIndex we have a connector that handles chunking and embedding calls.
[02:05] Mohammed Khan: And for embeddings, do you support the same model catalog? We want to align embedding vectors between our offline store and real-time features.
[02:14] Diego Alvarez: Yes, same catalog across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. You can pin model versions so embeddings are stable. We also expose vectorization latency metrics and token counts in traces.
[02:27] Samir Desai: Security — we need SOC 2 and ability to use our KMS for key wrapping. Also audit logs for every model call.
[02:36] Jamie Park: We're SOC 2 Type II. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. Audit logs are available; we stream them to S3 or your SIEM. We can show sample log entries after the call.
[02:51] Mohammed Khan: VPC peering — if we go Private we want the inference infra in our VPC or a private link. What's the model there?
[03:00] Diego Alvarez: We offer two Private modes: customer-managed VPC where the control plane runs in Redwood and inference nodes in your VPC via private endpoints, or fully on-prem package for air-gapped needs. For most customers we do VPC peering or PrivateLink.
[03:15] Ava Brooks: Latency again — you mentioned autoscaling. If we have a burst of traffic from a tenant is there pre-warm/burst capacity?
[03:25] Rina Patel: On Dedicated you can configure burst capacity and warm pools. For Hosted we have a cold-start cushion but Dedicated gives deterministic throughput because you have reserved GPUs.
[03:34] Mohammed Khan: Okay. Let's talk gateway/proxy. We currently run Envoy at the edge with a custom plugin that does tenant routing and early quota checks. We were thinking about using Redwood's gateway as a sidecar vs calling Redwood from our central gateway — pros/cons?
[03:50] Jamie Park: Two patterns we've seen: 1) Central gateway -> Redwood API: simplest, keep tenant logic on your side, Redwood enforces API-key quotas and billing. 2) Sidecar/gateway per cluster: reduces cross-net hops and enables local batching/prefix caching before hitting Redwood — this helps latency and costs.
[04:10] Diego Alvarez: With the sidecar pattern you can also maintain local KV cache for prefix queries and only hit Redwood for new context. We provide SDK hooks to integrate the cache layer.
[04:21] Mohammed Khan: Interesting. That matches our preference to minimize egress. Do you support mutual TLS between our Envoy and Redwood?
[04:29] Jamie Park: Yes — mTLS and customer certs are supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports IP allowlists and API keys, and we can extend with mTLS via private connectivity.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: Observability — we run Datadog and Splunk. How do we get traces and token-level cost?
[04:49] Diego Alvarez: We emit structured traces with traceparent headers and propagate your incoming trace IDs. Token-level cost breakdowns can be included as attributes on spans, and we have a plugin to ship those metrics to Datadog. We can also provide CSV exports for chargeback.
[05:04] Ava Brooks: On tracing, will the SDK automatically inject headers or do we need to wire it manually?
[05:10] Rina Patel: SDK can auto-inject if you pass the trace context, or you can call our helper to attach tags. For LangChain callbacks we surface a callback that captures streaming tokens and spans.
[05:22] Mohammed Khan: What about quotas for streaming sessions? If someone keeps a stream open and pumps tokens, do you count in real time?
[05:31] Diego Alvarez: We meter streaming tokens as they're emitted. Quotas are token-based by default. For long-running streams you can set a maximum tokens/session and a per-minute rate cap.
[05:41] Lena Ortiz: Billing — does Redwood provide per-tenant invoices or do we get a consolidated bill and we do internal chargebacks?
[05:48] Jamie Park: We can do both. We typically send consolidated invoices but we can also export per-API-key usage to your billing system or SFTP. For Dedicated, we can surface tenant cost reports daily.
[05:58] Mohammed Khan: Another thing — LangChain's retriever pattern hits embeddings and re-ranks. Does Redwood support reranking and zero-shot reranks server-side to reduce client compute?
[06:12] Rina Patel: We have server-side reranking primitives — you can pass candidate embeddings and ask Redwood to do similarity scoring or scoring with a separate reranker model. That reduces round trips.
[06:22] Ava Brooks: Nice. For our PoC we'd like to test an end-to-end pipeline: chunking -> embeddings -> retrieval -> rerank -> generate. What's the minimum setup?
[06:33] Diego Alvarez: For a quick PoC: Hosted pilot + your gateway calling Redwood should be fastest. We'll provide the LangChain/LlamaIndex starter repo, a sample dataset, and we can run a small benchmark on p95 latency with a synthetic QPS you provide. If you need stable throughput, move to Dedicated for the pilot.
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: Timeline — we want a pilot in January. Stakeholders: Platform team (Mohammed), ML infra (Ava), Security (Samir).
[07:01] Jamie Park: Great — we can do a two-week Hosted pilot, then Dex can propose a Dedicated pilot if you want committed capacity. (laughs)
[07:10] Mohammed Khan: (laugh) Who's Dex?
[07:13] Jamie Park: Internal nickname. Ignore that.
[07:18] Samir Desai: Quick security flag: our compliance team will need the private deployment checklist and an overview of where logs are stored and for how long. Also SSO integration — we use Okta with SAML.
[07:29] Rina Patel: We have a Private deployment checklist and an SSO guide for Okta SAML/SCIM. We'll attach our SOC2 attestation and data retention options.
[07:38] Mohammed Khan: We also want to run a small benchmark — can Redwood support a local runner that hits your Hosted endpoint from our VPC to measure egress and network latency?
[07:49] Diego Alvarez: Yes — we can provide a small loadgen container and a script that runs from your infra hitting our endpoints. For precise network measurements we'd prefer PrivateLink, but basic benchmarking works over public endpoints too.
[07:59] Ava Brooks: One more: LlamaIndex connector — does it store vectors in our vector DB or can Redwood host ephemeral vectors to speed up rerank?
[08:09] Rina Patel: We support both. Many customers keep their vector DB (Pinecone/Weaviate/FAISS) and call embeddings. For hybrid mode, Redwood can host an ephemeral cache of top-K vectors to reduce round trips, but persistent storage is still recommended for reproducibility.
[08:25] Mohammed Khan: About SDK versions — how often do you push breaking changes that might affect LangChain adapters?
[08:33] Rina Patel: We keep the public SDK backward compatible for minor versions and publish migration guides for major versions. For LangChain adapters we version the adapter repo and tag compatibility. We'll run a smoke test with your stack before the PoC.
[08:45] Lena Ortiz: Any red flags in terms of lock-in? If we build this with Redwood and later move, how portable are our prompt libraries and embeddings?
[08:56] Jamie Park: Portability: prompts and embeddings are portable — embeddings are just vectors. For model-ops there are differences, but we expose model names and allow export of embeddings and logs. We also support pinned model versions so you can emulate behavior elsewhere if needed.
[09:12] Mohammed Khan: Pricing question: if we go Dedicated, do we still pay per-token for usage on top of the reserved capacity?
[09:21] Jamie Park: Typically Dedicated includes a baseline reserved compute. Above that you can be billed for overage tokens or we set higher commit tiers. We'll include burst pricing in the sheet.
[09:32] Samir Desai: For audit logs — retention policy? We need 1 year at the minimum, and ability to export for subpoena.
[09:41] Diego Alvarez: We have configurable retention; default is 90 days in the console, but for Enterprise/Private we can do 1 year or longer depending on plan. Exports are available as S3.
[09:53] Ava Brooks: Ops question — does Redwood provide an SDK to report custom metrics (like user_id, tenant_id) that show up in the per-request trace?
[10:01] Rina Patel: Yes — request metadata can include custom tags. We recommend tagging by tenant_id only, not PII. Those tags are available in traces and in the cost breakdown.
[10:12] Mohammed Khan: Can we run internal rate limiter using token-bucket on the client side and use Redwood quotas as the final guard?
[10:20] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely — that's a common pattern. The edge enforces a per-second limit and Redwood enforces daily and token caps.
[10:28] Lena Ortiz: Okay, let's map out immediate deliverables.
[10:31] Jamie Park: Action items recap — Mohammed will share VPC diagram, Rina will get the LangChain starter repo out, Jamie will send pricing, Diego will draft observability notes. We'll schedule the PoC kick-off first week of January.
[10:45] Mohammed Khan: Sounds good. Quick parking-lot question — do you support multi-tenant isolation within a single Dedicated cluster? We don't want noisy neighbor if we want to keep costs down.
[10:56] Diego Alvarez: Yes, Dedicated clusters support namespace-level resource controls and cgroup isolation. You can also carve GPU slices per tenant if needed.
[11:08] Ava Brooks: Fantastic.
[11:10] Jamie Park: Any other questions?
[11:14] Lena Ortiz: Nothing immediate. We'll review the materials and get the network folks to send diagrams.
[11:21] Jamie Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the repo links and pricing within two business days.
[11:28] Meeting end.
